name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz ~20% of pre-war traffic; blockade on
summary: Hormuz traffic about 20% of pre-war levels; Iraq reaches understanding with US on oil exports via a lane near Oman
state: Lloyd's List Intelligence puts Hormuz traffic at about 20% of pre-war levels, and UKMTO confirmed eight attacks in the strait and three in the Gulf in the week to 8 Nov, with three vessels sunk (The National). The Revolutionary Guards claim at least 12 ships have burned since the start of November, mostly after mine strikes; few such claims are independently confirmed (The National). Iraq reached an understanding with the US on 8 Nov to export oil through a lane near Oman (Asharq Al-Awsat). IMF PortWatch logged one transit on 1 Nov against a pre-crisis 85 a day (Gulf News), a far lower count than Lloyd's.
for_you: Crews and operators can follow UKMTO notices and flag-state advisories. Disruption at Hormuz tends to feed through to longer delivery times and higher freight and insurance costs, with import-dependent economies in Asia and Europe most exposed.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, at about 20% of pre-war levels per Lloyd's List Intelligence (8 Nov)

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
